records.title: Ginsenoside Rh2 Attenuates Post-Myocardial Infarction Heart Failure by Modulating the TGF-β/Smad2 Signaling Pathway.
records.abstract: Myocardial fibrosis and oxidative stress are key drivers of post-myocardial infarction heart failure (post-MI HF). Ginsenoside Rh2 (GRh2) has shown cardioprotective potential, but its role in post-MI HF and the underlying mechanism remain unclear. Mice with permanent left anterior descending artery ligation were treated with GRh2 (10 mg/kg/day, gavage) or enalapril for 28 days, cardiac function (echocardiography), fibrosis (histology/immunohistochemistry) and cardiac injury markers were assessed. Cardiac transcriptomes were sequenced to identify enriched pathways. H9C2 cardiomyoblasts and human iPSC-derived cardiac organoids were subjected to oxygen glucose deprivation (OGD) and treated with GRh2 with or without the TGF-β receptor agonist SRI-011381 (SRI), viability, oxidative stress, apoptosis, fibrosis and TGF-β/Smad2 signalling were measured. In vivo, GRh2 treatment markedly improved cardiac function and reduced myocardial fibrosis in mice with post-MI heart failure. Transcriptomic analysis revealed that the TGF-β signaling pathway was substantially enriched. In vitro, GRh2 treatment significantly improved cell viability and reduced oxidative stress and fibrosis in OGD-exposed H9C2 cardiomyocytes and cardiac organoids. These protective effects were strongly associated with the suppression of the TGF-β/Smad2 signaling pathway. GRh2 can improve myocardial function and alleviate fibrosis, oxidative stress and cell apoptosis after MI. In cells and organoids, these protective effects depend on the inhibition of the TGF-β/Smad2 signaling pathway, suggesting that this pathway is a potential mediator of the cardiac protective effect of GRh2.

records.title: Patient-Derived Organoids from cryopreserved tissue can represent clinically relevant tools for drug testing in Biliary Cancer.
records.abstract: Patient-derived organoids (PDO) are three-dimensional cultures established from cancer tissues. While PDOs can replicate morphology and drug sensitivity of cancer from given patients, their clinical applicability is limited by their lack of integration in clinical trials. We aimed to define the establishment rate of PDOs from patients with cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) and establish a protocol for the generation of PDOs from cryopreserved tissue. We established a biobank of PDOs from tumour tissues (N=26). A protocol for organoid establishment from cryopreserved tissue was optimised in mice, confirmed in human PDO, and validated across institutions. While we started from a wide enrolment of different subtypes, including Pancreatic cancer (N=7), CCA (N=11), duodenal (N=2) and Ampullary Cancer (N=6), we refined the protocol towards biliary phenotype, with reduced efficiency rate in intestinal phenotype cancers. In total, 15 PDOs were established (58%); in the CCA cohort the efficiency rate of 75% (8 out of 11). Confirmation of organoid tumour origin was achieved through pathology review within a clinically-relevant time frame [median: 1.6 months (0.43-4.83 months)]. There was no numerical enrichment of successful PDO establishment for CCAs with poor prognostic factors such as perineural invasion, vascular invasion, nodal status and resection margins (p>0.05). Data from drug screening was ready within an average of 3 months from tissue collection (range:1.4-3.4 months). PDO from cryopreserved tissue was successful in 67% of cases and maintained the morphology, secretory functions, kinetic and dynamic growth patterns, transcriptomics, and drug sensitivity compared to organoids established from fresh tissues. Cryopreserved tissue can facilitate the centralisation of PDO establishment and thus, the integration of biliary PDOs in multicentric trials.

records.title: Human brain cellular xenografts in neuroimmunology and beyond.
records.abstract: Human brain cellular xenograft (HBCX) models are emerging as a platform to study human brain physiology and pathology in vivo. HBCXs involve transplanting human pluripotent stem cell-derived neurons, glia, or organoids into immunodeficient mice to model human disease. These models have revealed human-specific cellular and molecular phenotypes, developmental trajectories, and disease mechanisms that would otherwise be inaccessible in traditional in vitro systems and animal models. They also provide a scalable, genetically editable framework for functional genomics studies, drug testing, and biomarker discovery. Given the pronounced species differences in microglia and other tissue-resident brain macrophages and their central involvement in neurodegenerative disease, these models also provide an in vivo platform to interrogate human neuroimmunology. In selected settings, they may help guide future cell-based therapeutic strategies. This review provides an overview of the current applications, discusses the challenges and limitations, and highlights future avenues of HBCXs in neuroimmunology and translational research.

records.title: Modeling somatic mutations associated with neurodevelopmental disorders using mosaic human brain organoids and assembloids.
records.abstract: Somatic mosaicism, the presence of genetically distinct cell populations within a single individual, has emerged as a key driver of human brain diversity and pathology. Originally associated with focal epilepsies and malformations of cortical development, recent evidence shows that somatic mutations can also contribute to neuropsychiatric and neurodegenerative diseases. High-throughput sequencing and single-cell multi-omics have revealed that the brain is a landscape of clonal expansions and somatic variants. To model the functional consequences of these mutations, new approaches are needed. This review focuses on emerging approaches that use human brain organoids and assembloids to model mosaic brain tissue and investigate cell-autonomous and non-cell-autonomous effects of genetic variants.

records.title: Alcohol disrupts spatial coordination of autophagy-lysosome pathways to impair intestinal barrier integrity.
records.abstract: Alcohol use disorder (AUD) drives intestinal barrier dysfunction, endotoxemia, and liver injury, yet the epithelial mechanisms remain undefined. Autophagy and lysosomes maintain intestinal epithelial homoeostasis and barrier integrity, but their response to chronic alcohol exposure is unclear. Human intestinal tissues from individuals with and without AUD were analysed alongside human intestinal organoids. Wild-type, CAG-RFP-EGFP-LC3, GFP-LC3B, and Atg16l1 hypomorphic mice underwent chronic-binge ethanol feeding. Organoids and Caco-2 cells were exposed to ethanol (50 mM) with or without bafilomycin A1 or Torin-2. Autophagy-lysosome pathways were assessed using transcriptomics, immunofluorescence, biochemical fractionation, and flux reporters. Alcohol induced heterogeneous autophagy-lysosome responses characterised by lysosomal stress/adaptive remodelling. These changes occurred with limited autophagosome formation and maturation, resulting in impaired autophagic throughput. These responses differed along the crypt-villus axis and between intestinal regions. Disrupted autophagy was associated with altered trafficking and accumulation of claudin-2. Atg16l1 hypomorphic mice exhibited increased baseline intestinal permeability vs wild-type controls (p = 0.03). Following ethanol exposure, Atg16l1 hypomorphic mice showed greater intestinal permeability (p = 0.003), circulating and hepatic endotoxin (p = 0.002), hepatic triglycerides (p = 0.01), and serum ALT (p = 0.02) vs ethanol-fed wild-type mice. Alcohol disrupts intestinal autophagy-lysosome homoeostasis in a spatially heterogeneous manner, accompanied by defective epithelial proteostasis and tight junction dysregulation. Impaired autophagosome formation exacerbates gut permeability and liver injury, supporting intestinal autophagy as a potential therapeutic target in alcohol-associated disease. Broader applicability of the human findings requires validation in larger cohorts. This study was supported by grants from the National Institutes of Health.

records.title: Multiplex Visualization of Oncoproteins in Cancer Organoids by Wide-Range NIR-to-Visible Lanthanide Emission.
records.abstract: In line with the Food and Drug Administration's (FDA's) initiative to reduce, refine, and potentially replace animal testing in drug development through New Approach Methodologies, including toxicity testing, cancer organoids are emerging as human-relevant platforms for preclinical drug screening. By enabling direct, quantitative multiplex imaging of multiple protein targets in cell-line-derived organoids, our lanthanide imaging toolkit (LIT) extends analysis from conventional monolayer cultures to physiologically relevant three-dimensional models and offers a scalable tool for mechanistic studies, drug screening, and preclinical development with reduced reliance on animals.

records.title: Single-Cell Whole-Transcriptome Detection Expands the Observable RNA Space for AI Virtual-Cell Models.
records.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing has supplied cell atlases and artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled virtual-cell models with scalable, gene-level descriptions of cellular state. Yet prevalent poly(A)-based counting assays capture only part of the RNA landscape. Here, "single-cell whole-transcriptome detection" denotes sequencing-based efforts to detect a broader range of RNA biotypes than conventional poly(A)-based gene counting; no assay detects or quantifies every cellular RNA species without bias. We compare RNA-capture scope, transcript-structure resolution, temporal labeling, spatial context, and additional modalities as distinct measurement dimensions. From a biosensing perspective, analytical sensitivity, transcript coverage, throughput, and assay bias determine which signals are available to computational models. We then examine cell-state representations, regulatory networks, dynamics, perturbation prediction, and foundation models. Total-RNA assays reveal additional non-coding RNAs, long-read methods inform transcript structure, and temporal assays constrain RNA kinetics. Whether these signals improve prediction beyond conventional gene-count inputs requires matched, task-specific model comparisons. We distinguish molecular observability, statistical association, predictive performance, and causal validation, which requires appropriate interventions. We propose benchmarks controlling sequencing depth, cost, model architecture, and held-out samples while testing feature ablations, out-of-distribution performance, uncertainty calibration, and experimental outcomes. Together, high-throughput poly(A)-based profiling and broader RNA measurements provide complementary cellular breadth and regulatory depth.

records.title: Virtual cells: progress and challenges from mechanistic modeling to data-driven integration.
records.abstract: Virtual cells aim to represent cellular states computationally and predict responses to genetic, chemical, environmental, temporal, and spatial conditions. For comparative purposes, this review uses state encoding (E), state transition (T), and observation decoding (D) as a conceptual abstraction spanning explicit mechanistic models, data-driven foundation and perturbation models, multimodal systems, and spatial and multiscale simulation. We examine model boundaries, data foundations, resource disclosure, out-of-distribution evaluation, causal evidence, and experimental validation. Independent benchmarks show that parameter count and training-set size do not automatically yield robust out-of-distribution generalization, while transcriptomic representations alone do not capture the full functional state of a cell. Trustworthy virtual cells will require perturbation-responsive transitions, cross-modal alignment, continuous-time dynamics, mechanistic constraints, calibrated uncertainty, independent experimental validation, and, where appropriate, closed-loop experimental feedback.

records.title: Progress of metabolomics-centric multi-omics research in medicine.
records.abstract: Metabolomics reveals molecular changes at the metabolic level during biological processes. Recent advancements, particularly through integration with other omics and artificial intelligence (AI), are advancing metabolic data analysis and multi-omics interpretation. This review introduces a "metabolomics-centric" paradigm as a conceptual framework for multi-omics integration, positioning metabolic readouts as the functional anchor for interpreting genotype-phenotype relationships. It also chronicles the evolution and medical applications of integration technologies. Our discussion first traces the field's evolution from bulk to single-cell and spatial methodologies, next surveys integration strategies to uncover mechanistic insights, and finally examines how AI-driven multimodal data integration and AI-optimized metabolomics workflows tackle persistent biological and computational challenges. Looking forward, this review identifies the AI virtual cell as a pivotal future direction for metabolomics-based multi-omics integration, calling for increased attention to its development to simulate dynamic molecular phenotypic networks within a multi-omics context.

records.title: Emerging frontiers for AI in single-cell genomics.
records.abstract: We are just over a decade into the single-cell revolution in biology, which has been coupled to the growing use of artificial intelligence (AI) in single-cell genomics. Most early single-cell RNA embedding models and subsequent "foundation models"-representational models pretrained on large single-cell datasets-did not gain wide traction among experimental biologists. However, as massive single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) atlas efforts ramp up, there is a clear rationale for exploiting AI models to interpret new datasets in the context of vast existing data resources. Meanwhile, the advent of single-cell epigenetic/multiomic assays and Perturb-seq technologies presents new opportunities for AI modeling. Here, we review AI embedding and foundation models for scRNA-seq and single-cell assay for transposase-accessible chromatin using sequencing (scATAC-seq), extensive machine-learning efforts to exploit single-cell multiome in regulatory genomics, and AI strategies to learn "virtual cell" models from Perturb-seq, ending with a description of current limitations of single-cell AI models and an outlook for future advances.

records.title: Benchmarking biological knowledge-graph priors against single-cell foundation models for Perturb-seq prediction.
records.abstract: Perturb-seq prediction increasingly relies on either biological graph priors or single-cell foundation models, but their relative value is difficult to interpret when architectures, split definitions and graph sources vary simultaneously. We benchmarked STRING functional associations and Gene Ontology co-annotation against dense, self-edge-only and exact-degree-rewired supports in one fixed graph-attention backbone, with a separate 200-HVG STRING-GO-control-co-expression sensitivity. Four public Perturb-seq datasets, three nested gene-space scales and three optimisation seeds were evaluated on held-out guide conditions; GEARS, scGPT and Geneformer were evaluated on the same held-out conditions, output-gene panels and Pearson-r metric after model-specific validity checks. At 200 highly variable genes, STRING-GO improved the equal-dataset Pearson r by +0.016 (95% interval [+0.010, +0.022]) relative to dense support. Dataset effects were positive in Adamson (+0.017), Norman (+0.015), Replogle K562 (+0.017) and Replogle RPE1 (+0.014), and 122/200 guide conditions improved (0.61 [0.54,0.68]). The top-20-gene Jaccard difference was +0.009 [+0.006,+0.012]. STRING-GO exceeded self-edge-only support by +0.024 [+0.018,+0.029] and the mean of ten exact-degree rewires by +0.011 [+0.005,+0.017]. The native-panel effect declined from +0.016 at 200 genes to +0.009 at 1000 genes; the 1000-200 interaction was -0.006 [-0.011,-0.002]. The primary graph-support comparison was formulated and conducted during peer-review revision rather than planned as an a priori confirmatory study. All three external models passed implementation-specific checks. Across 36 protocol-matched dataset-scale contrasts, 32 were within the descriptive ±0.030 reference envelope and four were outside, all favouring the external model. These results demonstrate a modest empirical predictive improvement under the evaluated matched protocol; they do not by themselves establish practical biological relevance.

records.title: AI-enabled fungal biomanufacturing: from genome mining to the artificial intelligence virtual cell.
records.abstract: Fungi are important chassis organisms for sustainable biomanufacturing owing to their strong secretion capacity, metabolic diversity, and adaptability to industrial processes. Driven by the rapid development of Artificial Intelligence (AI), computational approaches that enable machines to learn patterns from data and make predictions, together with omics technologies and synthetic biology, data- and model-driven strategies are increasingly reshaping fungal cell factory design and optimization. This review summarizes recent advances in AI-enabled fungal biomanufacturing, covering AI-assisted genome mining, enzyme and pathway analysis, genome editing, metabolic network modeling, and intelligent fermentation control. The review further highlights the emerging concept of the artificial intelligence virtual cell (AIVC), which integrates multi-omics data, mechanistic modeling, and machine learning-based approaches into a unified multiscale framework for simulating dynamic cellular behaviors. The technical foundations and potential applications of AIVC in fungal metabolic engineering, drug discovery, agriculture, and environmental biotechnology are reviewed. Finally, key challenges-data quality and standardization, cross-scale model integration and interpretability, and the gap between in silico prediction and experimental validation-are highlighted. This review provides a systematic perspective on the role of AI and virtual cell technologies in advancing next generation fungal biotechnology.

records.title: Shared α-helix chimeraffibodies enable linker-free bispecific protein design.
records.abstract: Small protein scaffolds enable precise targeting but often rely on flexible linkers that increase conformational heterogeneity and immunogenic liabilities. Here we develop Chimeraffibodies (CABs), a linker-free bispecific scaffold class that encodes interdomain geometry through seamless α-helix sharing. CABs are designed by AlphaSync, a structure-design framework that defines domain orientation through closed-form exhaustive local rigid-body superposition and ProteinMPNN-based sequence refinement. Using HER2-binding affibody and an albumin-binding domain, we generated 861CM, which preserved parental paratopes while enforcing a defined shared-helix architecture. Structural, biophysical and cellular analyses demonstrated stable assembly, cooperative target recruitment and retained affinity, with HSA binding of ∼14.3 pM and HER2 binding of 610 pM in the albumin-bound state. In vivo imaging revealed sustained tumor localization, reduced hepatic and renal background and improved organ-to-tumor contrast. CABs establish helix sharing as a geometry-encoded strategy for generating compact, homogeneous, and pharmacokinetically optimized bispecific proteins.

records.title: EquiDesign: a versatile computational framework for de novo protein sequence design.
records.abstract: Designing amino acid sequences that uniquely fold into target three-dimensional conformations defines the protein inverse folding problem, a formidable bottleneck in de novo protein design. Current computational paradigms, including deep learning-based approaches, often struggle to reconcile high sequence accuracy with structural stability, computational efficiency, and generalizability across diverse protein families. Here, we present EquiDesign, a deep learning framework that surmounts these constraints via a novel multistep Equiformer-enhanced architecture. By disentangling geometric features into invariant scalars and equivariant vectors, EquiDesign preserves the intrinsic directional topology of the protein backbone during message passing. This is achieved through spatial K-nearest neighbor graph construction and geometric attention mechanisms that hierarchically fuse multiscale contextual information, yielding a physically grounded representation of protein conformations. Extensive benchmarking demonstrates that EquiDesign achieves superior sequence recovery on standard and challenging test sets compared with state-of-the-art methods. Critically, the generated sequences exhibit exceptional structural fidelity, folding stability, and sequence diversity, as validated by comprehensive controls against training-set memorization, compositional bias, and physical energy landscapes, alongside targeted diversity sampling. These results establish EquiDesign as a robust, scalable, and generalizable inverse folding solution, driven by SE(3)-equivariant encoding and multiscale geometric attention, thus propelling de novo protein design toward unprecedented structural precision.

records.title: Building a Physically Interpretable Compressed Chemical Space via Grid-Based Optimization.
records.abstract: In recent years, deep generative models have been increasingly adopted for molecular optimization and design. In many such models, molecules are encoded into latent spaces that provide compact representations of their features. However, these latent spaces remain difficult to interpret in physical terms, and it is unclear how much structural and molecular information is retained under compression. This limitation becomes especially important when molecular behavior depends on specific three-dimensional arrangements embedded in an environmental context. Here, we introduce COMPRESS (Compression Of Molecular Physical fields into Reduced Spatial Sites), an optimization framework that represents a small molecule using a fixed number of physically parametrized spatial sites. Each site is defined by three spatial coordinates and three interaction parameters, yielding a fixed-size representation that remains directly interpretable in physical terms. To preserve molecular information, COMPRESS representations are optimized to reproduce the density, electrostatic, and van der Waals fields of the corresponding all-atom molecule on discretized three-dimensional grids. We systematically evaluate how molecular information is retained as the number of sites, K, is reduced. Our analysis covers benzene, 20 chemically diverse chemical scaffolds, benzene dimers, protein-ligand complexes, and 10,000 molecules chosen from the GEOM-Drugs data set. Across systems, field agreement deteriorates slowly at high resolution and then undergoes a rapid, pronounced transition at lower resolution. We further find that K = 25 conformers capture about 97% of the molecules from GEOM-Drugs under a loss threshold of 0.05, which we use as an indicator of fidelity. These results show that COMPRESS can provide a fixed-size, physically interpretable molecular representation, enabling compression to be evaluated directly using molecular interaction fields and resulting physical quantities. We also introduce a decoder that reconstructs all-atom structures directly from a COMPRESS representation, showing that the representation can support molecular generation in addition to field-preservation analysis. Finally, rationally modified COMPRESS representations through changes to site charge and size or the addition or removal of sites are shown to generate realistic chemical compounds upon decoding.

records.title: Programming N-linked glycan composition through de novo protein design.
records.abstract: N-linked glycans are ubiquitous post-translational modifications that mediate diverse biological processes, including cell signaling and adhesion, molecular recognition, and host-pathogen interactions. Despite their importance, N-linked glycans have largely remained beyond the reach of biomolecular design due to a lack of methods capable of jointly modeling glycans and protein structure. Here, we develop a general all-atom computational pipeline for creating de novo glycoproteins in which the amino acid sequence encodes both the location and composition of N-linked glycans. The method uses three-dimensional protein structure to tune glycan accessibility to processing enzymes in the eukaryotic secretory pathway. Systematic increases in steric restriction progressively reduced processing, shifting glycans from heterogeneous complex-type structures toward increasingly underprocessed oligomannose-type species resembling those found on many viral glycoproteins. Despite this programmed restriction, the resulting oligomannose glycans remained accessible for biological recognition, inhibiting uropathogenic Escherichia coli adhesion to human bladder cells and binding mannose-binding lectin. These results establish steric control of N-glycan processing as a genetically encodable design principle and extend computational protein design to functional glycoproteins with programmed composition.

records.title: The physical foundation beneath protein generative modeling.
records.abstract: Physical equations in protein modeling appear to have been replaced by generative models trained directly on structure data. By learning a mapping from noise to data, sampling de novo protein structures has become much more efficient. However, such models can also learn non-physical features and break down with out-of-distribution settings which are typical in protein design campaigns. In this review, we highlight where the physics persists in protein generative modeling pipelines and the issues that linger when physically relevant components of a macromolecular system are left unmodeled. We present a perspective that respecting the underlying physics of macromolecular systems, increasingly through learned representations that are physically grounded and updating generative models with experimental data, is foundational to generative modeling for functional protein design.

records.title: De novo design of ligand binding proteins using large language models alone.
records.abstract: Protein design has rapidly advanced with the advent of sequence- and structure-based machine learning models. However, reasoned design, which applies physicochemical principles and rules derived from sequence-structure-function relationships, has not seen the same benefits from generative machine learning models. Here, we test the ability of common large language models (LLMs; e.g. Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini) to consider design principles to generate de novo proteins that bind metals and lipophilic small molecules without copying existing sequences. Common LLMs alone are able to 1) generate protein sequences to adopt a desired fold and bind the target ligand and 2) explain the principles that motivate the design choices. Following structure prediction and filtering, we selected a small set of designs (6 to 12 designs per query) for experimental validation, affording metal binders in one round of LLM-based design (25% hit rate) and perfluorooctanoic acid binders in two rounds (25% hit rate in the second round of design). Importantly, the LLMs produce detailed justification to accompany the de novo designed sequences, providing a conceptual framework on which designs can be evaluated. While the successful designs have some deviations from the prompted parameters and LLM-articulated design rationale, these campaigns provide a case study that highlights the utility of LLMs in making protein design more comprehensible and accessible to users without sophisticated design expertise.

records.title: [Genomic alterations in thymic epithelial tumors: State of knowledge, and the interest of liquid biopsy].
records.abstract: In the absence of randomized phase III trial data, thymic epithelial tumors (TETs) are rare malignancies of the prevascular mediastinum managed according to the WHO histological and the Masaoka-Koga classifications. Next-generation sequencing has revealed distinct mutational characteristics between thymomas, which are characterized by a low tumor mutational burden and a near-specific GTF2I mutation, and thymic carcinomas which are dominated by alterations in CDKN2A, TP53 and KIT. These findings open the way for novel therapeutic strategies, involving immune checkpoint inhibitors and multi-kinase inhibitors in advanced thymic carcinomas. Notwithstanding the potential of liquid biopsy as a non-invasive monitoring tool, specific biological obstacles in TETs currently limit its clinical applicability. Recent confirmation of the interest of liquid biopsy in perioperative management of lung cancer raises the prospect of transferring this approach to TETs. The key challenge lies in identifying the biological marker most suited to the monitoring of longitudinal tumors. Genomic profiling of TETs enhances (rather than supplants) the historical histological classification, and should progressively inform therapeutic stratification, particularly in cases of thymic carcinoma.

records.title: The role of circulating gene variants in penile carcinoma.
records.abstract: Penile squamous cell carcinoma (PSCC) is highly prevalent in low- and middle-income countries and is associated with significant rates of morbidity and mortality. Lymph node involvement is the most critical predictor of survival, making management approaches essential for improving oncological outcomes. Despite advancements in minimally invasive staging techniques, no accurate method for detecting lymph node involvement has yet been developed. While resecting positive lymph nodes is crucial for patient survival, lymph node dissection can lead to considerable morbidity. This study aims to identify circulating gene variants that could assist in detecting positive lymph nodes in patients treated for PSCC. We employed liquid biopsy and next-generation sequencing to identify circulating variants in 42 genes associated with tumor development and progression. This analysis included 21 men who underwent total or partial penectomy and inguinal and/or pelvic lymphadenectomy. We found that patients with lymph node metastases exhibited a significant higher number of circulating gene variants. An unexpected finding was the presence of uncommon pathogenic variants in the NF1 gene in the majority of patients. In conclusion, the detection of a higher number of circulating variants may help in selecting patients for inguinal and/or pelvic lymphadenectomy, ultimately improving cure rates and reducing morbidity. Furthermore, the high prevalence of pathogenic variants in NF1 gene suggests that this variant have a crucial role in the carcinogenesis processes and may serve as biomarkers for diagnosis and/or predisposition to PSCC.

records.title: CRISPR/Cas13a-Regulated SERS Biosensor Based on Plasmonic-Enhanced Magnetic Rods with Intensified Electromagnetic Field Generation for Breast Cancer Associated miRNA Detection.
records.abstract: Early and sensitive detection of breast cancer biomarkers is essential for improving patient prognosis, yet rapid and amplification-free analysis of low-abundance circulating miRNAs remains challenging. Herein, we report a CRISPR/Cas13a-regulated surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) biosensor, termed the CaRER sensor, for on-site detection of miRNA-511-5p, a clinically relevant breast cancer-associated biomarker. To enhance plasmonic activity and SERS performance, Ag, known for its strong SERS amplification capability, was incorporated into Au-Ni-Au magnetic rods to construct plasmonic-enhanced magnetic rods (PEMRs), which generated markedly stronger Raman signals than conventional Au-Ni-Au rods. Integration of PEMRs with the CRISPR/Cas13a system enabled amplification-free and highly sensitive detection through target-triggered trans-cleavage-induced modulation of the SERS signal after sequence-specific recognition of miRNA-511-5p. The CaRER sensor achieved femtomolar-level detection with high selectivity and reproducibility, and reliably distinguished clinical plasma samples from breast cancer patients and healthy controls. In addition, the magnetic properties of PEMRs enabled efficient separation and robust signal readout, improving assay practicality and operational reliability. The incorporation of Au also enhanced antioxidative stability relative to Ag-dominant plasmonic structures, supporting long-term chemical stability and sensing reliability. Owing to the programmability of crRNA, this platform can be readily adapted to diverse nucleic acid biomarkers through simple sequence redesign, highlighting its potential as a versatile point-of-care testing (POCT) tool for cancer diagnostics and liquid biopsy applications.

records.title: Bridging the Gap - Translating AI in Pathology into Clinical Impact.
records.abstract: AbstractHematoxylin and eosin-stained tissue analysis has remained the global foundation of diagnostic pathology since the 19th century, and recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) now enable the extraction of clinical and molecular insights from routine images. Yet only 5 of the 1430 AI- and/or machine learning-enabled medical devices cleared by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration are modern pathology AI tools based on whole-slide images, whereas 1094 are classified in the radiology category. Furthermore, only approximately 4% of U.S. slide volume is currently read digitally. We argue that this disconnect reflects a hierarchy of barriers to clinical impact: foundational infrastructure and economic hurdles, postdigitization challenges related to sample variability and clinician trust, an underdeveloped implementation and governance pathway, and persistent equity gaps in low- and middle-income settings. Against this backdrop, two near- and medium-term translational pathways stand out: AI as a digital copilot for clinical evaluation and AI-enabled clinical trial design. Together, these approaches offer measurable workflow and trial-enabling benefits, with the potential to improve patient outcomes.

records.title: Cost-effectiveness of capivasertib plus abiraterone for PTEN-deficient metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer in the United States.
records.abstract: On June 12, 2026, the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved capivasertib (Truqap; AstraZeneca) in combination with abiraterone and prednisone for adult patients with metastatic androgen pathway modulation-naive or -sensitive (mAPMN/S) prostate cancer, corresponding clinically to metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (mHSPC), that is PTEN-deficient as detected by an FDA-authorized test. The pivotal CAPItello-281 trial demonstrated a statistically significant radiographic progression-free survival (rPFS) benefit (hazard ratio [HR] 0.81; p = 0.034) but a nonsignificant and immature overall survival (OS) benefit (HR 0.90; p = 0.401). Capivasertib carries a publicly available list price of approximately $23,762 per 28-day cycle. To estimate the incremental cost-effectiveness of capivasertib plus abiraterone and prednisone versus abiraterone and prednisone alone, both with androgen deprivation therapy (ADT), from the perspective of a US third-party payer. A three-state partitioned survival model (PSM) was developed with a lifetime horizon (40 years), 4-week cycle length, and 3% annual discount rate. Individual patient-level survival data were reconstructed from published Kaplan-Meier curves via the Guyot algorithm. Given OS immaturity and AIC differences of less than 1 point across six parametric families, a preregistered proportional hazards (PH) base case was applied: the trial OS HR of 0.90 was applied to the placebo parametric fit. Generic abiraterone, ADT, companion diagnostic, and monitoring costs used National Average Drug Acquisition Cost (NADAC) or Medicare reimbursement schedules; capivasertib used a publicly available list-price proxy, and the OS hazard ratio was sampled lognormally in PSA. Uncertainty was characterized via one-way sensitivity analysis, eight pre-specified OS extrapolation scenarios, four scenario analyses, and probabilistic sensitivity analysis (PSA; n = 10,000). Reporting followed CHEERS 2022 standards. Capivasertib accrued 4.103 discounted QALYs at a total discounted cost of $1,455,507, versus 3.703 QALYs at $207,230 for abiraterone alone. Incremental cost was $1,248,277 and incremental QALYs 0.400, yielding an ICER of $3,120,720 per QALY. The probability of cost-effectiveness was 0% at willingness-to-pay thresholds of $100,000, $150,000, $200,000, and $500,000 per QALY. The most favorable OS extrapolation scenario (log-normal) yielded an ICER of $1,359,445 per QALY. The ratio of mean incremental cost to mean incremental QALY across PSA iterations was $3,148,744 per QALY; because a minority of iterations (13.54%) yielded a negative incremental QALY, the distribution of individual iteration ICERs is uninformative, and uncertainty was characterized using the cost-effectiveness acceptability curve and plane. At current list pricing, capivasertib plus abiraterone is not cost-effective for PTEN-deficient mHSPC from a US payer perspective. The result is structurally driven by high incremental drug acquisition cost and small incremental QALY gain under immature and nonsignificant OS data. Mature OS data and a major net-price reduction would likely be required for cost-effectiveness.

records.title: A dual signal amplification photothermal biosensor based on Sn-CDs/NPC and DNA walker for prostate cancer cell detection.
records.abstract: A target-driven DNA walker photothermal sensor based on Sn-doped carbon dots loaded onto N-doped nanoporous carbon (Sn-CDs/NPC) was constructed for highly sensitive detection of prostate cancer cells LNCaP. Fe3O4@Apt/S3 served as a capture unit to specifically recognize and capture Prostate-Specific Membrane Antigen (PSMA)-overexpressing LNCaP cells, releasing the trigger strand S3. Fe3O4@S1/S2@Sn-CDs/NPC was designed as a signal unit, where S3 hybridized with S1 and initiated the Exo III-assisted DNA walker cyclic amplification strategy, continuously releasing the photothermal probe Sn-CDs/NPC. Following magnetic separation, the photothermal signals generated by the released Sn-CDs/NPC under 808 nm NIR laser irradiation were positively correlated with the concentration of LNCaP cells. Under optimized conditions, the cell quantification biosensor exhibited a linear range with a detection limit as low as 9 cells/mL, along with excellent selectivity, reproducibility, and storage stability. In spiked real blood and urine samples, the recoveries ranged from 95.2% to 98.6% and 95.5% to 104.8%, respectively. This technology integrates advantages of simple operation, high sensitivity, and low cost, providing a new technical pathway for early liquid biopsy of prostate cancer and holding promise for advancing the clinical translation of precision cancer diagnosis.
